correctness.rationale: For n=product p_i^{alpha_i}, the discrepancy separates exactly into the sum of gcd(k,alpha_i)-log_2(alpha_i+1). For k=1 every term is nonpositive and vanishes exactly at alpha_i=1; prime powers give divergence to -infinity. For k>=2, choosing a prime r|k and arbitrarily many exponent-r prime factors gives t(r-log_2(r+1))->+infinity because 2^r>r+1, while exponents kt+1 give gcd(k,kt+1)=1 and discrepancy 1-log_2(kt+2)->-infinity. All quantifiers and boundary k=1 are covered.

value.rationale: The claim directly resolves the basic global boundedness question singled out by the introducing paper and sharpens it to a complete signed-range dichotomy. The constructions expose a structural contrast between k=1 and k>=2 rather than a finite numerical curiosity: repeated exponent equal to a prime divisor of k forces positive divergence, whereas exponents congruent to 1 modulo k force negative divergence. This is a motivated exact fact about the new function, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
